kpis.label: Reference price
kpis.sub: Upper band Rs 245 (49,02,000 fresh shares, Rs 120.10 cr). At Rs 245: market cap Rs 400.3 cr post-issue; P/E 13.7x on FY26 PAT on post-issue shares (9.6x on pre-issue shares; 8.4x on the company's EPS of Rs 29.13, which excludes the Jul-2026 loan-conversion shares); P/B about 1.75x post-issue; EV/EBITDA about 6.4x. RHP peer Seemax Resources 16.1x. Objects floor Rs 222.

focus.title: Related-party capex & subsidiaries
focus.detail: Disclosed promoter-group dealings: 642 MHE units bought from Watrana Traction Company for Rs 25.21 cr in FY26 (28% of FY26 capex; units it had earlier hired to the company), hire charges paid to it Rs 18.42 / 19.35 / 12.08 cr, batteries and spares from Watrana Traction Pvt Ltd Rs 4.76 / 7.74 / 10.88 cr, and a Rs 62 cr corporate guarantee from that company. Watrana Traction Pvt Ltd is in the same line of business; a non-compete agreement is dated 12-Aug-2025. The RHP states the promoters have no interest in the vendors quoting for the issue-funded equipment (p. 98).

focus.title: Auditor qualifications / changes
focus.detail: PRASS & Associates LLP restated opinion carries an emphasis of matter (not a qualification) on the switch from WDV to straight-line depreciation from 1-Apr-2023, which raised FY24 PBT by Rs 12.05 cr. Fleet is depreciated over the Schedule II 15-year life.

focus.title: Valuation model guard
focus.detail: AMBER: DCF and relative diverge by -46.9% - the divergence is the finding; name its cause

focus.title: Valuation model guard
focus.detail: RED: objects floor sits above blended fair value

focus.title: Valuation model guard
focus.detail: AMBER: TV above 75% of EV - DCF is mostly a terminal guess

focus.title: Data gap (medium)
focus.detail: Cost of fleet units sold through trading income (whether ex-fleet machines' book value sits in cost of sales); split of the FY26 trading margin

comfort.title: Bonus issue / share-count consistency
comfort.detail: Share count reconciles: 10,000 shares on incorporation; 1,000:1 bonus on 28-Sep-2024 (1.001 crore shares, on which the restated EPS of Rs 18.03 / 24.41 / 29.13 is computed); 14,28,500 shares allotted on 27-Jul-2026 at Rs 245 to the two promoters on conversion of Rs 35.00 cr of interest-free director loans, giving the pre-issue 1,14,38,500. The conversion is after the reporting date, so EPS excludes it; our P/E uses the full pre-issue and post-issue counts.

comfort.title: Cash flow vs profit
comfort.detail: Cumulative CFO Rs 115.10 cr against cumulative PAT Rs 71.64 cr over FY24-26 (161%). Free cash flow is negative because fleet capex (Rs 52.83 / 44.28 / 91.18 cr) exceeds CFO; borrowings funded the gap (debt Rs 93.12 cr to Rs 164.08 cr).

comfort.title: Current vs deferred tax
comfort.detail: FY26 tax Rs 10.02 cr on PBT Rs 39.18 cr (25.6%): current Rs 6.93 cr, deferred Rs 3.09 cr. The deferred charge arises from faster tax depreciation on the fleet (DTL Rs 8.13 cr), usual for an equipment owner.

comfort.title: Objects arithmetic as price floor
comfort.detail: Objects: Rs 98.13 cr for 323 MHE, 12 AWPs and 688 batteries (FY27 Rs 58.89 cr, FY28 Rs 39.23 cr), from unrelated vendors' quotations; no orders placed yet. GCP is capped at Rs 10 cr, so at Rs 245 issue expenses are at least about Rs 12 cr (10% of the issue). Objects floor computed by the model.

comfort.title: Customer / supplier / geographic concentration
comfort.detail: Customers are spread: largest customer 3.33% and top ten 25.70% of FY26 revenue (5.89% / 33.73% in Q1 FY27), 357 customers. Supply side more concentrated: top five suppliers 56.37% and top ten 64.81% of FY26 purchases. All revenue is from India; logistics and warehousing 21.55% of FY26 sales.

comfort.title: Contingent liabilities
comfort.detail: Contingent liabilities and commitments Rs 9.29 cr at 30-Jun-2026, of which capital commitments Rs 6.88 cr and LCs Rs 1.82 cr. One civil matter of Rs 16.00 cr names the company: an LLP-partner dispute in Futuristic Bots LLP (promoter group) against the promoters; the Delhi High Court vacated its interim order on 28-Oct-2026 and appointed an arbitrator. Tax matters Rs 0.05 cr.

comfort.title: Monitoring agency
comfort.detail: Monitoring agency appointed: Infomerics Valuation and Rating Ltd (agreement 5-Nov-2026).

comfort.title: SME conditions
comfort.detail: In-principle approval from NSE Emerge dated 27-Oct-2026; issue 30.00% of post-issue capital.

reverse.sentence: The price asks the business to deliver 26.1 times its current free cash flow, in perpetuity.

levers.label: Lever 1 - implied perpetual growth on current FCFF
Lever 2 - implied WACC at terminal g
Lever 4 - required NWC % of revenue (steady state)

overhang.label: Promoters' minimum contribution (20% of post-issue capital)

strengths: Revenue up 62% in two years; PAT Rs 29.16 cr (p. 223)
Spread customer base: top ten 25.70% of revenue, 357 customers (p. 163)
weaknesses: Fleet growth debt-funded; borrowings 1.92x net worth at Mar-26 (p. 222)
Free cash flow negative after fleet capex
Labour-heavy model: employee cost 43% of revenue, 3,883 staff (pp. 157, 223)
opportunities: Indian MHE rental market USD 2.33 bn in 2026, 13% CAGR to 2036 per the company-commissioned Infomerics report (p. 134)
AWP rental (33 units) as a second line
Issue-funded 323 MHE and 12 AWPs over FY27-28 (p. 88)
threats: Rental-rate competition from OEMs and other renters
Promoter group runs a same-line business (non-compete in place, p. 213)

adjustments.reason: Rs 0.26 cr one-off charge for the new labour code notified 21-Nov-2025; adding it back raises recurring profit.

adjustments.item: Liabilities no longer required written back
adjustments.reason: Rs 0.05 cr in FY26 (Rs 0.01 cr in FY24) of non-recurring write-backs in other income.

adjustments.item: Profit on sale of fleet machinery in other income
adjustments.reason: Rs 0.23 cr in FY26. Disposal of old units is part of running a fleet, so shown for information only.

Director loans averaged about Rs 11.8 cr in FY25 and Rs 29.0 cr in FY26 and carried no interest. Rs 35.00 cr was converted into shares on 27-Jul-2026 at Rs 245, and those shares are in our share count, so the saving does not recur as an earnings gap; shown for information. FY24 not computed (opening balance not given).

adjustments.item: Depreciation method changed from WDV to straight line (FY24)
adjustments.reason: The switch raised FY24 PBT by Rs 12.05 cr (depreciation Rs 7.43 cr instead of Rs 19.48 cr); the auditor notes it as an emphasis of matter. Straight line over the Schedule II 15-year life is the policy going forward and the FY25-26 effect is not disclosed, so it is not deducted from recurring earnings; it does make FY24 not comparable with earlier years.

adjustments.item: Step-up in trading margin on machinery and battery sales
adjustments.reason: Sale of machinery, batteries and spares Rs 19.05 cr in FY26 against stock-in-trade cost Rs 8.90 cr: a gross margin of Rs 10.15 cr, up from Rs 3.94 cr in FY25. The Rs 6.21 cr rise is about the whole of the FY26 PBT increase (Rs 6.33 cr). The restatement notes say some sold machines were reclassified from fixed assets to stock-in-trade, so part of this may be disposals of fleet units; the RHP does not split it. Shown for information.

earnings_quality.verdict: Reported P/E is a fair measure: the adjustments found move FY26 PAT by +0.5%, within the 10% threshold. On the FY24-FY26 average, which smooths one-year items, the P/E is 16.8x reported and 16.7x adjusted.
flags: Rs 0.26 cr one-off charge for the new labour code notified 21-Nov-2025; adding it back raises recurring profit.
Rs 0.05 cr in FY26 (Rs 0.01 cr in FY24) of non-recurring write-backs in other income.
checked: Gratuity and leave provisions booked on actuarial valuation, rising with headcount (Rs 0.90 cr and Rs 0.24 cr in FY26; p. 224)
Doubtful-debt provision steady at Rs 0.19 cr; no write-back (p. 235)
No R&D, borrowing costs or pre-operative expenses capitalised; intangibles Rs 0.08 cr (p. 222)
Director remuneration Rs 0.24 cr in FY26 for the two executive promoters (p. 238); no market-rate figure, so no adjustment
Hire charges to the promoter group fell from Rs 19.35 cr to Rs 12.08 cr after the company bought those units (p. 332): a structural saving, not a one-off
